sermon.title: Understanding Hate and Persecution
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer recaps the seasons of the last days and then turns to recognizing hatred and persecution. From John 15 and Second Timothy 3:12 he says believers are hated for following Jesus and living godly, shows that John the Baptist, Jesus and Stephen were killed for speaking morally, recounts early martyrs, the Inquisition and modern persecution, and urges American Christians to stand for Bible morality.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: At 0:20 he cites “First Corinthians 12 38” for the children of Issachar; the passage is in 1 Chronicles 12 (verse 32), which is linked. At 6:58 he cites “Acts 3 18” for Jesus remaining in heaven until all things are restored; that is Acts 3:21 (Acts 3:19-21 is linked). At 16:50 he says the martyr in the arena was arrested in “2003 A.D.” as spoken; the dates and details of the martyrdoms (from Foxe’s Book of Martyrs, as he says), the Inquisition dates and the quotation about the Constitution are given as spoken and have not been checked.

chunks.short_answer: He tells of a 22-year-old new believer with a nursing infant whose father and husband urged her to renounce Christ; she would not, and was given to the wild beasts. faqs.question: Does persecution start in your own family?
faqs.answer: He says it starts in their own family: the more you want to serve God and do what is right, the more people want to separate from you, and your friends change.

faqs.question: Will wisdom be restored in the church?
faqs.answer: From Daniel 12 he says the wicked shall not understand but the wise shall understand, so there is going to be a restoration of wisdom.

faqs.question: Are wars and earthquakes signs of the end?
faqs.answer: He says many end time prophets focus on wars, earthquakes, famines and plagues, but Jesus said that is not a sign of the end; it is just going to happen.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not troubled; for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.

faqs.question: What are two biblical reasons Christians are persecuted?
faqs.answer: He says when we have an encounter with Jesus to follow him, and when we live godly in this present world, people are going to mistreat us.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.

faqs.question: What is the top reason Christians are persecuted?
faqs.answer: He says speech is the top one: when you start talking about and living Bible morality, they are going to hate you and persecute you.

faqs.question: Can Christians hide that they are Christians?
faqs.answer: He says Christians are exposed when they live morally; you cannot hide the fact that you are a Christian.

faqs.question: For what beliefs did the Inquisition persecute people?
faqs.answer: He says people were persecuted for saying the Bible is the only source of God’s truth, the cup and bread are not Jesus’ body and blood, penance is not necessary, and for rejecting idols, the mass and indulgences.

faqs.question: Did Protestants also persecute others?
faqs.answer: He says Protestants turned around and did what had been done to them, persecuting Catholics, Protestants and pagans over sacraments and baptisms and different doctrines.

faqs.question: What should American Christians flee?
faqs.answer: He says they need to flee the public opinion of legalizing sin, crime and immorality, get in a group that embraces morality, and get America back to being great.
